title: The first superconducting final focus quadrupole prototype of the FCC-ee study

predicted_errors.error_location: Quench protection paragraph ("A 50 Ω crowbar connected to a 75 Ω dump resistor")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated resistances are physically impossible for a magnet operating near 1 kA: a 75 Ω dump resistor carrying ~765–1000 A would develop 57–75 kV across the magnet terminals, far beyond any realistic insulation/protection design (and a 'crowbar' is by definition a low-impedance bypass). These values are almost certainly milliohms; as written the protection circuit described cannot work.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract ("higher-order multipoles below 1 × 10⁻⁴ units") vs. Results ("below 1 unit in the central region")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In accelerator-magnet convention one 'unit' already equals 10⁻⁴ of the main field, so '1 × 10⁻⁴ units' corresponds to 10⁻⁸ relative, i.e. four orders of magnitude smaller than the value quoted in the body ('below 1 unit'). The abstract and results therefore disagree by a factor 10⁴ (or the abstract misuses the unit definition).

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract: "Field quality is excellent, with higher-order multipoles below 1 × 10⁻⁴ units, consistent with simulations and room temperature tests."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The results section states the cold field-quality results are 'worse than the warm tests' and that undesired harmonics on the corrected edge reach 'values below 5 units'. Claiming a blanket bound on all higher-order multipoles and full consistency with the room-temperature measurements overstates the reported data, especially since the warm-test correction step (45° magnet rotation) was not repeated cold.

predicted_errors.error_location: Field-quality discussion: "This approach can also get rid of crosstalk from the adjacent magnet in a twin aperture arrangement as envisaged in FCC-ee."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: No twin-aperture configuration was built or measured in this work; the conclusion itself states that crosstalk compensation 'will be demonstrated' in future work with an HTS sextupole. The assertion that the method 'can get rid of' crosstalk is therefore unsupported by any evidence presented.

predicted_errors.error_location: Field-quality discussion: "This validates the possibility of tuning the conductor layout of CCT magnets in the edge to remove undesired higher-order multipole content."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The measurements show residual higher-order harmonics up to ~5 units on the corrected side, i.e. a reduction, not removal. 'Remove' overstates the demonstrated effect.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 caption vs. text reference to Table 2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'The correction is confirmed by comparing coefficients from the coils positioned on the corrected and non-corrected sides as shown in Table 2', while the Table 2 caption describes a comparison 'between the warm and cold (1.9 K) measurements' at 5 A and 765 A. The table content described in the caption does not match the comparison the text attributes to it.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction: "Its specifications are summarized in Table 1"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 1 is cited for the prototype specifications (lengths, currents, field strength), but no Table 1 is present in the paper, so key quantitative parameters (nominal current, aperture, field gradient) cannot be verified against the text (e.g. the 765 A measurement current, 1000 A short-sample current, >20% margin).

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction: "following a similar work done at CERN [2]"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors are themselves at CERN, and the acknowledged collaborators providing CCT/impregnation expertise are at PSI; attributing the precursor CCT work to CERN is inconsistent with the rest of the paper and suggests a misattributed reference.
